questions.prompt: An import discovers an application account. What remains separate?

options.text: Matching and confirming its association to the intended identity
options.explanation: Discovery alone does not prove ownership or approved linkage.

options.text: Whether the account appeared in discovery
options.explanation: That limited observation is already supplied.

options.text: Whether every user must be newly created
options.explanation: An import can encounter existing records.

options.text: Whether the imported data performs browser authentication
options.explanation: Import and sign-in are different operations.

questions.prompt: Before interpreting an import's results, what should be established?

options.text: The connector, direction, included population and operation scope
options.explanation: A count is meaningful only for the actual population and operation.

options.text: Only the import's friendly display name
options.explanation: A label does not describe all filters and relationships.

options.text: Only whether another integration succeeded
options.explanation: A different connector has a different scope.

options.text: Assume every source record is always included
options.explanation: Filters and configured boundaries can limit discovery.

questions.prompt: Two records share an email string. What is needed before linking them?

options.text: The approved matching rule, uniqueness and sufficient ownership evidence
options.explanation: A matching-looking string is not a complete identity biography.

options.text: Always merge records based on that string alone
options.explanation: Mutable or reused values can be ambiguous.

options.text: Pick the record with more permissions
options.explanation: Privilege is not identity proof.

options.text: Assume duplicate names imply duplicate people
options.explanation: Several records can legitimately describe one person.

review.heading: A matching rule is a comparison, not a biography

questions.prompt: An application already has the intended user's account before onboarding. What should the integration consider?

options.text: A supported and verified match to the existing resource
options.explanation: Do not assume every assignment needs a new target account.

options.text: Create a duplicate before inspecting the existing account
options.explanation: That can add ambiguity and unnecessary resources.

options.text: Delete the old account without an ownership review
options.explanation: An existing record may hold legitimate data and access.

options.text: Treat account existence as proof all permissions match
options.explanation: The target's actual state still needs checking.

questions.prompt: An import matches two existing identities under the proposed criteria. What is appropriate?

options.text: Stop the automatic link and resolve the ambiguity through the approved process
options.explanation: Arbitrary selection risks associating the wrong person and account.

options.text: Choose the first result by default
options.explanation: Result order is not ownership evidence.

options.text: Choose the identity with the newer display name
options.explanation: Recency of a label does not establish the correct match.

options.text: Create a third identity automatically
options.explanation: Another record does not resolve the existing ownership question.

review.heading: Recognize when the evidence is insufficient

evidence: Candidate identities: user A and user B

questions.prompt: Why inspect sourcing consequences before confirming an imported association?

options.text: The supported association may affect which system maintains certain data
options.explanation: Linking records can have consequences beyond displaying them together.

options.text: A match can never affect ownership or lifecycle
options.explanation: That depends on the integration's supported behavior.

options.text: The importing source always owns every attribute automatically
options.explanation: Attribute ownership must be verified rather than generalized.

options.text: Matching automatically validates all user passwords
options.explanation: Record association is not credential validation.

questions.prompt: A search returns the first page of accounts. What is unsafe to conclude?

options.text: That an unlisted account is absent from the full result set
options.explanation: Inspect pagination and search scope before making an absence claim.

options.text: That the displayed accounts were returned on this page
options.explanation: That limited observation is directly established.

options.text: That more pages may need inspection
options.explanation: That is precisely the relevant follow-up.

options.text: That target IDs can identify returned resources
options.explanation: Object IDs remain useful within their supported scope.

review.heading: Read the whole result, not just its first page

questions.prompt: During an identity integration review, what does reconciliation compare?

options.text: Expected records or relationships with the observed current state
options.explanation: It identifies differences that need interpretation and verified follow-up.

options.text: Only whether the sign-in page loads
options.explanation: Page availability is not a record-state comparison.

options.text: Only the number of assigned apps in every tenant
options.explanation: Scope and intended relationships are necessary, not one universal count.

options.text: Only whether every discovered record should be deleted
options.explanation: Discovery does not authorize a universal destructive action.

questions.prompt: An import proposes many more removals than expected. What should happen first?

options.text: Check scope, source availability and the proposed impact before confirming
options.explanation: An anomalous count is evidence to investigate, not automatic authorization.

options.text: Approve because the connector generated the proposal
options.explanation: Generated intent does not establish correct lifecycle scope.

options.text: Assume every employee actually left
options.explanation: The count alone does not prove employment changes.

options.text: Delete duplicates in unrelated apps immediately
options.explanation: That broad action is unsupported by the supplied observation.

review.heading: Treat an unexpected removal count as evidence

evidence: Import filters, source scope and availability: not yet checked

questions.prompt: How does an import differ from just-in-time account creation during sign-in?

options.text: They are different triggers and processes with their own supported matching and lifecycle rules
options.explanation: Do not infer one operation's behavior from the other.

options.text: Every import requires the user to authenticate interactively
options.explanation: Import is not inherently a user browser sign-in.

options.text: JIT always replaces all later reconciliation needs
options.explanation: Account and lifecycle state still require supported management.

options.text: Both automatically prove target resource permissions
options.explanation: Neither operation alone establishes every authorization outcome.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.

questions.prompt: A dry-run matching preview selects an account, but no confirmation is supplied. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether the association was actually confirmed and became effective
options.explanation: Preview demonstrates proposed matching, not completed linkage.

options.text: Whether the preview selected a candidate
options.explanation: That observed candidate is supplied.

options.text: Whether every preview creates a target user
options.explanation: Preview should not be equated with actual resource creation.

options.text: Whether an account's display name must be globally unique
options.explanation: Display names are not a universal identity uniqueness guarantee.

review.heading: A matching rule is a comparison, not a biography

questions.prompt: After confirming an approved match, what should be verified?

options.text: The actual identity-resource association and any resulting profile, assignment or lifecycle effects
options.explanation: A completed link needs verification of its intended and relevant downstream consequences.

options.text: Only whether the confirmation button was clicked
options.explanation: An action request is not a complete outcome check.

options.text: Only an unrelated successful import
options.explanation: Different operation evidence cannot verify this association.

options.text: Only whether both users share a department
options.explanation: Department resemblance is not sufficient ownership evidence.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
